done_when: Each task and fix keeps one worker chat per tool from its first round to merge: a later round resumes it even after a model or effort change, a Forge or machine restart, or a fresh worktree of the same item; a fresh chat starts only when the recorded chat truly can't be resumed (the tool reports it gone, or the item moved to the other tool), and then the round says why in one line; plan reads keep their reader chat across rounds the same way; the coordinator guide says so; command tests with stubbed Codex and Claude cover each resume case and each fresh-chat reason, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Not done — A failed v1.2.2 Codex read starts a fresh chat after upgrade despite its original chat remaining resumable. New evidence beyond the earlier upgrade finding: `tests/fixtures/forge-v1.2.2/src/forge/story.py:231` clears the JSON identity to null after a failed read, while `codex.py:389` in that fixture retains the conversation ID in the turn log. This guard treats those null keys as an existing identity and prevents log recovery; `preserve_chats` at current `src/forge/codex.py:223` also skips the record. Consequently, upgrade sync preserves no binding, and the next read never attempts the original ID. Erasing metadata after sync loses even the recoverable log. Proof test 7 starts its failed reads with current Forge, and the native earlier-release reader proofs start with successful reads, so neither covers this case.
findings.title: Not done: Recover earlier-release reader chats after failed reads

findings.body: Raise: Not done — An earlier-release task that successfully returned to Claude after a Codex fallback loses its Claude chat on upgrade. The new evidence is that v1.2.2 records can legitimately contain both identities: its worker fallback at `tests/fixtures/forge-v1.2.2/src/forge/worker.py:128` runs Codex, whose `codex.py:360` preserves the Claude field; a subsequent successful Claude round updates that field at `worker.py:414` without removing the Codex identity. That release writes no worker routing field (`worker.py:115`). Upgrade preserves both IDs, but this inference always selects Codex when both exist. Lines 114–116 then clear the still-valid Claude session and start another without attempting to resume it. The tool-change ruling does not cover this case: the last successful round already used Claude, and the configured tool is unchanged. Native earlier-release worker proofs exercise one fix round on one provider, so they miss this normal split-worker recovery sequence.
findings.title: Not done: Preserve the active tool in earlier-release mixed worker records

stop.reason: Owner wants every in-flight fix finished; narrowed to the two remaining findings: Codex's real missing-rollout wording, and reader chats archived by an earlier release

why: Worker chats should be reused: each task or fix should keep the same worker conversation from its first round until it merges, but today some rounds start a fresh chat (for example when the model or effort changes, after Forge restarts, or when a record is missing), losing context and costing tokens (owner, 2026-10-09)
